# Security defaults

<!-- Generated by scripts/security-defaults.ts from packages/server/test/security-defaults-table.ts: run `npm run docs:security-defaults` after changing a default. -->

What `tabularius serve <folder>` does when you give it nothing else, setting by setting, what changes each one, and what goes wrong if you change it. A test starts a server with no flags and checks every row against what it really does, so this page cannot drift from the program. [The threat model](threat-model.md) says who these defaults are meant to hold against.

"Checked by" says how a row is held: **probed** means the test asked the running server (or looked at a file it made); **read from code** means the value is a constant or a line of source that the test reads, because nothing on a running server shows it from outside.

## Network and transport

| Setting | Default | What changes it | If you change it | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Listen address | This computer only (127.0.0.1) | `--host 0.0.0.0` (or an address), `TABULARIUS_HOST`, which also needs HTTPS or `--allow-plain-http` (next rows); `--https <domain>` listens on every address unless `--host` says otherwise. `tabularius service install` listens on this computer only too unless its `-- --https <domain>` option is given (every address then), and applies the same rule to `--host`. The PostgreSQL-protocol port (`--sql-port`) listens on the same address | Anyone who can reach the machine can reach the sign-in pages. Set an admin password and use HTTPS before listening on the network | probed |
| HTTPS | Off: plain HTTP | `--https <domain>` (certificate from Let's Encrypt), `--https local` (the folder's own authority), `--tls-cert` with `--tls-key`, or a proxy that does HTTPS | Without it, passwords and session tokens cross the network in the clear. On this computer alone that does not matter | probed |
| Listening beyond this computer without HTTPS | Refused: the server does not start, and says how to fix it | HTTPS (`--https`, `--https local`, `--tls-cert` with `--tls-key`) lifts it. `--allow-plain-http` (or `TABULARIUS_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP`) allows plain HTTP for a proxy or network you control; the server then warns in the log unless `--public-url` starts with `https://`. The Docker image sets it, because the port you publish decides who can connect | Allowing it sends passwords and session tokens across the network in the clear to anyone who can see the traffic | probed |
| Page security headers | On: no sniffing, no framing, no referrer, a content security policy (checked on the web client; the admin console's policy allows its own inline scripts), and a Permissions-Policy on every response that denies the microphone, payment, USB, serial, HID, Bluetooth, MIDI, screen capture, motion and orientation sensors, WebXR, idle detection and ad-topics APIs. The camera and location stay available to the web client's own pages only (Insert from Device, Get Current Location) | Not switchable | None to change; they stop other sites framing the pages and the browser guessing types, and keep a page that gets script into it from asking for a device the product never uses | probed |
| Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) | Sent for one year on every response served over HTTPS (directly, or through a proxy on this computer or in `--trusted-proxies` that says `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`); never over plain HTTP. No `includeSubDomains`, no `preload` | Not switchable. It follows how the request arrived | After a browser has seen it, it will not open this name over plain HTTP for a year, and a certificate error cannot be clicked through. Keep the certificate renewing before you serve a name over HTTPS | probed |
| Cross-origin access from other websites | None for the Data API and the console, and `/mcp` refuses a browser origin. The OAuth endpoints (`/oauth/*`, where AI apps register and sign in) answer any origin | `--mcp-origin` (repeatable) or `TABULARIUS_MCP_ORIGINS` for `/mcp`; the Data API has no switch (a page on another site cannot call it) | Allowing an origin lets a page from that site act with the signed-in person's rights | probed |
| Client address headers from a proxy (X-Forwarded-For and the like) | Not believed: the address that connected is the client, and a request that carries a forwarding header is not taken for one from this computer (the console refuses it) | `--trusted-proxies <addresses>` with `--proxy-header <name>` | Trust only proxies that overwrite or append the address they actually observed. An overly broad trust list lets clients forge audit, allow-list and rate-limit identities. See Client address attribution below | probed |

## Sign-in and accounts

| Setting | Default | What changes it | If you change it | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Admin console password | None set: the console opens from this computer only, and refuses a request addressed to any other name | `tabularius admin-password <folder>`; the console's own Settings | With a password set the console is open to whoever can reach the port and knows it; turn on HTTPS first. A sign-in lasts 12 hours (cookie `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`; over HTTPS it is named `__Host-tabularius_admin` and is `Secure`) | probed |
| File accounts with no password (FileMaker's default Admin) | Work from this computer only; refused from the network | `--allow-blank-passwords`; a file's own allowance for private-network addresses (`allowBlankPasswordFromLan`, in the console); `tabularius passwd <folder> <database> <account>` gives one a password | Allowing them means anyone who can reach the server can sign in as that account, with its privileges | read from code |
| Anonymous access | None: every Data API, web client and SQL route needs an account. A file converted by this version keeps its built-in [Guest] account switched off, even if the FileMaker file had it on (the conversion report says so); switched on, it still signs nobody in until it is given a password | Nothing needed. [Guest] can be switched on in Manage Security, and the privilege review then lists it; giving it a password makes it a shared account. Accounts with no password are the other way in (above) | A shared account is only as private as its password. A file that grants a privilege set to a blank-password account is open to this computer's users | probed |
| List of hosted files for people who have not signed in | Off: the list answers only a caller who signs in, with the files that account can open | `--list-files-publicly`, `TABULARIUS_LIST_FILES_PUBLICLY` | File names are visible to anyone who can reach the server | probed |
| Lockout after wrong passwords | 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes lock that account for 15 minutes; 30 failures from one address lock the address | Fixed values (`LOCKOUT` in `packages/store/src/sign-in-failures.ts`); an administrator can lift a lock in the console. This computer's own address has no address budget | Lower numbers lock people out more easily; higher ones let a stranger guess more | probed |
| Session idle time | 15 minutes for Data API and web client sessions; 15 minutes for Admin API tokens | Admin console Settings, or `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/session-timeout` (1 to 1440 minutes), for Data API and web client sessions only; Admin API tokens stay at 15 minutes; the web client can have its own | Longer sessions leave a signed-in browser or script usable for longer if it is left or taken | probed |
| Password rules for file accounts and the admin console | A new password needs at least 12 characters, for a file account (unless the file's own policy says otherwise) and for the admin console. Nothing expires. The lockout above is the other brake on guessing | `tabularius privileges <folder> <database> policy [minLength [maxAgeDays]]` for one file (0 for no minimum, a number of days to make passwords expire); `TABULARIUS_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` for the default (0 for none), which also sets the admin console's minimum | Lowering it accepts short passwords that a guesser, or a stolen password hash, gives up fast. Accounts that already have a shorter password keep it until it is changed; while any minimum is in force a blank password is refused as well (the empty password a converted file's account keeps still works from this computer only) | probed |
| API tokens (`ohbt_`) made for an account | Expire after 90 days (a calendar feed address, 365), and can write, unless made read-only or given another lifetime | Chosen when the token is made (`--expires-days` or `expiresDays`, 1 to 3650 days; `readOnly`, surfaces, layouts), or for every new one except calendar feeds with `TABULARIUS_TOKEN_DEFAULT_DAYS`; the console lists and revokes them | A token that leaks works until it expires or someone revokes it. A token cannot be made without an expiry. Tokens made before every token had to expire have none: they no longer work and the console lists them as needing to be made again | probed |
| Two-factor sign-in for [Full Access] accounts | Not required (available) | Per file, in the console or Manage Security (`requireTotpForFullAccess`) | Without it a stolen Full Access password is enough | probed |
| Single sign-on (OpenID Connect, LDAP) and SCIM provisioning | Off: no provider is configured, and SCIM answers 401 without a per-file provisioning token | `--oidc-issuer` with `--oidc-client-id` (or `--oidc-config`), `--ldap-url`; the console makes a SCIM token (valid 90 days unless 1 to 3650 is asked for, then a new one is needed) | A provider that signs in anyone with an email address needs `--oidc-trust-email` thought through; a SCIM token can create accounts until it expires or is turned off | probed |
| AI connector (`/mcp`) | Needs a credential from everyone, this computer included. A request addressed to a host name the server was not told (no `--public-url` or `--https` for it) is refused with 403 before the token is checked; a request without a token to this computer's own address or `localhost` gets 401. The server makes an administrator token on first start and keeps it in `.openhbam-mcp-token` in the hosted folder, readable only by the account that runs the server (`tabularius mcp-token <folder>` prints it) | `--mcp-token` (or `TABULARIUS_MCP_TOKEN`) sets the administrator token instead; an account (HTTP Basic), an API token from the admin console or Manage Security, or the OAuth sign-in limit a caller to one account's privilege set. Deleting `.openhbam-mcp-token` and restarting makes a new one. Give a cluster or a standby pair the same `--mcp-token`, so every process and a server that takes over accept the same one; the admin console is a separate door and trusts this computer until it has a password | Whoever holds the administrator token can read and change every hosted file: keep the file and the token out of repositories and chats. On Windows the file has no owner-only mode, so keep the hosted folder's own permissions tight | probed |

## What can reach outside

| Setting | Default | What changes it | If you change it | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AI assistant | Off: it needs `--ai` and a key. A key in the environment (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) does nothing on its own | `--ai` with a key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `~/.openhbam/anthropic-key` or `--ai-key-file`); per file, `tabularius ai <folder> <database> off`; `--ai-exclude` | With it on, questions and what the assistant reads go to the provider. A file switched off with `tabularius ai <folder> <database> off`, or named by `--ai-exclude`, is never sent. The AI-visible policy (next row) is a different thing: turning it off removes the refusal to read secret-named fields | probed |
| Token budget for one assistant question | 300,000 tokens (as billed: cached input at a tenth), strict: before each model call the worst it could add is reserved (text counted cautiously, a pasted picture as 5,000 tokens, and a margin when the provider's tool search is used), so a call that could pass the budget is not made | `--ai-run-tokens N` or `TABULARIUS_AI_RUN_TOKENS`: a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000 | A higher number lets one question, or a loop of tool steps, spend more of the day and month limits. The budget cannot be switched off (zero, fractions, 1e308 and numbers above 10,000,000 are refused at start), and there is no dollar budget for one question (the monthly one is `--ai-monthly-budget`) | probed |
| Per-file AI-visible policy | On for files made by Tabularius; off for converted and existing files | `tabularius ai-policy <folder> <name> on\|off`; the console | Off lets an AI operation read secret-named fields | probed |
| Outbound mail | Off: Send Mail never sends | `--send-mail` with `--mail-from` and an SMTP account (`TABULARIUS_SMTP`); `--test-outbound` captures mail instead of sending it | Scripts can send mail as the server | probed |
| Network access for scripts (Insert from URL, plug-in requests) | Off for every file, including a new or converted one and the demo, until an administrator turns it on. When on, loopback and the machine's own network are still refused unless listed; metadata and link-local addresses are always refused | The admin console's Script network switch for one file (Hosted files); `--allow-script-network` for every file; `--allow-script-network-to <hosts or ranges>` | A script can reach whatever the server can: mail, SMS and payment services, other machines on the network | probed |
| Web hosts a web viewer may load | None for every file, including a new or converted one and the demo: a web viewer shows only its own content (HTML a solution builds), and an address on the web shows as text. A listed host loads over https only, in a frame with no access to the app | The admin console's Web viewers may load list for one file (Hosted files) | A host on the list sees the address of whoever opens the page, and can show them anything, including a page that looks like the app's own | probed |
| Scripts installing plug-ins (Install Plug-In File) | Off | `tabularius plugins <folder> script-install on\|off` (stored as `scriptPluginInstall` in the folder's settings file) | A script (and so whoever can run it) could add code that runs in the server | read from code |
| Plug-ins | None installed; the bundled BaseElements-compatible set is built in and runs in the sandbox | `tabularius plugins`; the console's Plug-ins page (administrators only) | A plug-in the administrator installs runs with the permissions its manifest asks for; see docs/writing-a-plugin.md | probed |
| Webhooks and inbound hooks | Off: set up in the console, they do nothing until the server is started to allow them | `--allow-webhooks`, `--allow-inbound-hooks` (app connections have `--allow-app-connections` and are not probed here) | Webhooks send record changes to the address an administrator typed; inbound hooks answer calls from outside | probed |
| PostgreSQL-protocol SQL port for BI tools | Off | `--sql-port` | Another listening port to protect; read-only unless `--sql-writes` is also given, signs in with file accounts | probed |
| SQL writes over the PostgreSQL-protocol port | Off: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are refused (SQLSTATE 25006) | `--sql-writes` with `--sql-port` | A reporting or ETL account can change records, within its record and field privileges and the audit log; a connection inside BEGIN holds the file until it ends, goes idle for 30 seconds or reaches 5 minutes | read from code |
| Standby servers following this one (replication) | Off: the replication routes answer 404 | `--replication-token` (at least 16 characters) | The token lets a holder copy every hosted file | probed |
| Telemetry and update checks | None: nothing is sent to the project or anyone else on its own | Nothing to change; `tabularius upgrade` fetches only when run | This row only checks that the start-up log mentions no telemetry; the full list of outbound connections is the no-phone-home work (r21-06), not this table | probed |

## Limits

| Setting | Default | What changes it | If you change it | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size of one Data API request | 10 MiB of JSON; larger answers 413 (error 960) | Not switchable | Larger bodies hold memory while they are read | probed |
| Size of a file import in the web client | 50 MiB plus 256 KiB for the request around the file | Not switchable | Larger uploads hold memory while they are read | read from code |
| Picture thumbnails: passthrough size and limits on the converter programs | A picture is sent as it is only up to 128 KiB (and no bigger than the thumbnail asked for); the converter (pdftoppm, or sips on macOS) gets 20 seconds and, on Linux only, is run with prlimit (or ulimit in sh) at 512 MiB of address space, 20 seconds of CPU and 16 MiB for a file it writes | Not switchable; `TABULARIUS_THUMBNAILS=builtin` turns the converter programs off | On macOS and Windows the converter has no address-space, CPU or file-size limit beyond the 20-second timeout, the 16 MiB input cap and two converters at a time | read from code |
| Excel workbooks, plug-in packages, Notion ZIPs and BE_Unzip archives read from an uploaded file | At most 4096 entries; no entry may unpack to more than 1000 times its compressed size; an Excel XML part may nest at most 64 levels; at most 256 MiB unpacked from a workbook and 20 MiB from a plug-in package | Not switchable | A small file can be built to unpack to gigabytes or to thousands of parts; the file is refused whole, before anything is imported or installed | read from code |
| Time one request may hold the server | A minute; then it is stopped (error 812) | `TABULARIUS_REQUEST_BUDGET_MS` (0 for none) | Without a limit one slow request can stall everyone else | read from code |
| What one account, agent or session can pile up | 1,000 API tokens that work per account, 500 changes waiting for approval per approval-gated agent, 3 debugger runs or recordings at a time per session; past a limit the call is refused (error 812) and says what to do | Not switchable | Without a limit one account or agent could fill the file with tokens or proposals, or fill the disk with debugger copies | read from code |

| Setting | Default | What changes it | If you change it | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Audit trail | On: every record created, changed, deleted or duplicated is logged; reads are not logged; kept without limit | `logReads`, `redactSensitive`, `excludeFields` and `retentionDays` in the file's audit settings (console) | Logging reads grows the log fast; a retention limit deletes history; there is no switch to turn record logging off | probed |
| Backups | On: every day, the last 7 kept, in `Backups` beside the files, not encrypted (the console reports each one's check; this row probes the schedule, count and encryption only) | `--backup-every`, `--keep`, `--backup-dir`, `--no-backups`; `TABULARIUS_BACKUP_KEY` encrypts; `--backup-s3` copies off-site | A backup folder on the same disk is lost with it; an unencrypted one holds every record and every password hash | probed |
| Encryption at rest for the hosted files | Off: files are ordinary SQLite files | `tabularius encrypt <folder>` with `TABULARIUS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Anyone who can read the folder can read the data; passwords are stored as scrypt hashes either way | probed |

## Client address attribution

Tabularius uses the canonical socket address unless both `--proxy-header` (`TABULARIUS_PROXY_HEADER`) and `--trusted-proxies` (`TABULARIUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES`) authorize forwarding. Loopback is **not implicitly trusted**. Existing installations using only `--proxy-header` must add their proxy IPs/CIDRs, including loopback where appropriate. No fixed hop-count setting is needed: traversal starts at the socket, then walks the selected header **from right to left**, continuing only while the current hop is trusted. The first untrusted hop is the client. This follows the trusted-list method in [MDN: X-Forwarded-For](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Forwarded-For#selecting_an_ip_address), “first non-matching address”.

For a three-proxy chain, configure all three proxies. The last proxy is the socket peer; the two preceding proxies are the rightmost header entries. Earlier client-supplied entries cannot override the first untrusted address. Every trusted proxy must overwrite its header or append the peer it actually observed; network controls must prevent bypassing that proxy. Trust only the specific addresses/subnets you administer, not a whole client network.

| Input / use | Expected Tabularius result | Public basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No selected header or an untrusted socket peer | Canonical socket address; never a caller-selected address | [RFC 7239 §8.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7239#section-8.1), “cannot be relied upon to be correct” |
| X-Forwarded-For / Forwarded lists and repeated fields | Preserve wire order, validate the entire list, then walk trusted hops from the right | [RFC 7239 §§4,7.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7239#section-7.1); [MDN X-Forwarded-For](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Forwarded-For#parsing) |
| Forwarded parameters | Parse tokens and quoted strings, including quoted separators/escapes; require one IP-valued for parameter per element; reject duplicate names case-insensitively | [RFC 7239 §4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7239#section-4), “MUST NOT occur more than once” |
| Ports and brackets | IPv4:port or [IPv6]:port; decimal ports 1–65535; bare IPv6 has no inferred port. Forwarded requires quoting colon-containing values | [RFC 7239 §6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7239#section-6); the numeric port range is a Tabularius restriction | <!-- known-difference-ok: "inferred" here means no port is assumed for a bare IPv6 address; it is not a FileMaker comparison -->
| Unknown/obfuscated nodes, zones, empty elements, invalid ports or malformed syntax anywhere in the list | Socket fallback for attribution and edge accounting. Empty-list/parameter and zone rejection are deliberately stricter application policy | [RFC 7239 §§6–7](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7239#section-6) defines node forms; it does not require these Tabularius acceptance policies |
| X-Real-IP | Exactly one address; reject lists/repeated values | [nginx ngx_http_realip_module](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_realip_module.html#real_ip_header) describes the address header; single-value rejection is Tabularius policy |
| IPv6 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 | Normalize case, compression and padding; both dotted and hex mapped IPv4 become dotted IPv4 | [RFC 5952 §§4–5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5952#section-4); [RFC 4291 §2.5.5.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291#section-2.5.5.2), “IPv4-Mapped IPv6 Address” |
| Limits and lockouts | One key per IPv4 address or IPv6 **/64** (first four normalized hextets); rotating interface identifiers cannot create another bucket. OAuth registration, account-import IP limits, edge admission, account lockouts and shared address-limit consumers use the same function | Tabularius policy, using [RFC 4291 §2.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291#section-2.3) prefix notation; /64 is not an RFC-mandated abuse limit |
| Audit and allow-list attribution | Keep the full canonical address; do not replace it with the /64 bucket. Capture once per request, including delayed finish callbacks | Tabularius policy based on [RFC 5952 §3.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5952#section-3.2) matching concerns |

**Fallback is not permission to authenticate as the proxy.** A configured proxy with a missing or invalid selected header receives HTTP 400 before application authentication, retaining its socket identity for edge accounting. A forwarded client that resolves to loopback is rejected the same way. Forwarding headers on a loopback connection nobody configured as a proxy (a reverse proxy on this computer that was never named in `--trusted-proxies`) are not believed: that visitor is unknown, never this computer, and authentication answers it (the console refuses, `/mcp` answers 401). The refusals prevent malformed attacker-controlled prefixes retained by a proxy from acquiring local-only or blank-password privileges or the local address-budget exemption. Direct local callers sharing a configured proxy address must use a separate listener/configuration; the proxy-facing listener requires a valid header. The 400 says what to check and is logged (at most once a minute); it is Tabularius policy, not RFC or Claris requirements.

The cluster front resolves attribution once, overwrites `x-tabularius-peer` and `x-tabularius-forwarded`, and sends them over its private worker transport. Workers preserve the canonical address and trusted-forwarding provenance rather than parsing the external chain again. Address keys are identical across routes and workers; existing in-memory counters keep their existing process scope. Edge connection counts remain at the front, OAuth registration routes to the leader, and account authentication retains existing worker routing.

### KNOWN

| Unknown / limitation | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Claris forwarding-header trust, malformed-header behavior, and IPv6 grouping | **Unverified**; no Claris behavior is claimed documented or equivalent | <!-- known-difference: Server operation ;; Whether Claris Server trusts forwarding headers, how it treats malformed ones and how it groups IPv6 addresses is unverified; Tabularius applies its own strict profile ;; Address attribution, limits and lockouts behind a proxy may differ from FileMaker Server ;; A Claris Server run behind a proxy with valid, malformed and IPv6 forwarding headers -->
| Whether an operator's proxies overwrite/append correctly, or alternate ingress paths bypass them | Deployment-specific; synthetic tests do not establish this |
| Distributed aggregation of every application counter across workers/servers | Not added; this change makes identity keys consistent, not all counters global |
| Compatibility with optional empty Forwarded elements, obfuscated identifiers, zone IDs or port zero | Intentionally rejected by this strict Tabularius profile |


## Owner decisions

Defaults that are weaker than they could be, left as they are because changing them changes what people already rely on. Each says what would be done.

- **Admin console is open to this computer until a password is set.** On a shared computer any local user can open the console, and from it make `/mcp` tokens and act as the administrator, so a console password is what keeps the others out. Recommended: ask for the password on first visit even from this computer when the folder is not under the user's home directory. Not done: it would stop `tabularius` (no arguments) opening the welcome page straight away.

## Not covered

- Settings that only exist when something else is on (for example the OpenID Connect options, the SQL port's accounts, a standby's token): each is off by default, and the row for the thing that turns it on is above.
- What a plug-in an administrator installs can do: see [the threat model](threat-model.md).
- A crafted `.fmp12` file given to the converter: whether it can harm the server process has not been audited here.
- The browser: a computer or browser that is already compromised can do what the signed-in person can.
- How safe a password is. Only the minimum length is checked (the password rules row); nothing checks strength.
